correctness.rationale: Conjugation by Sym(A) preserves precisely block-size multisets, so the target quantifier reduces exactly to realizing every weak k-composition of N as sums of indivisible weights a_i. For sufficiency, if S >= (k−1)(a−1), each weak target composition of S+a has a bin of size >=a, so removing a and applying the prefix induction gives a representation. Conversely a failed index a_j=a with S<(k−1)(a−1) yields an obstruction: if N<=k(a−1), a target with all bins <a; otherwise k−1 bins of a−1 leave too small last capacity for all remaining >=a weights. Greedy a_j=1+floor(S_{j−1}/(k−1)) saturates the maximal capacity recurrence; truncating the last weight and using order-independent sufficiency proves every intermediate N. Independent enumeration of 414 weight multisets, with all weak target compositions, agreed with the criterion for small N,k; infinite family is proved analytically.

value.rationale: Universal support partitions are natural in permutation/orbit-refinement questions, and the finite support-budget exact criterion and sharp capacities answer a quantitative optimization question not supplied by qualitative infinite-atom existence results. The k=2 binary subset-sum criterion is classical and is explicitly excluded from a novelty claim; all-k optimal capacity is the motivating result.

final_claim: For finite nonempty atom set A, k>=2 and support partition R with nondecreasing block sizes a_1..a_b, R refines some conjugate of every target Q having <=k blocks iff for all j (k−1)(a_j−1)<=sum_{i<j}a_i; maximal support capacity for b blocks is G_k(0)=0, G_k(b+1)=G_k(b)+1+floor(G_k(b)/(k−1)), and minimum b for N atoms is min{b:G_k(b)>=N}.
limitations: Finite nonempty distinguishable atom set, k>=2, full permutation group, target partitions into <=k blocks; no infinite Fraenkel–Mostowski choice principle or infinite-cardinality generalization.
